question: Which of the following is the Chief Minister of a state in India primarily responsible for? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (07/08/2025) Shift 1)
options: President of India
Supreme Court
State Legislative Assembly
Governor of the State
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is State Legislative Assembly

Explanation:
According to Article 164 of the Indian Constitution, the Chief Minister is collectively responsible to the State Legislative Assembly. The Chief Minister is the head of the state government and leads the Council of Ministers. Although appointed by the Governor, the Chief Minister's appointment depends on proving majority in the Legislative Assembly. If the Chief Minister loses the confidence of the Assembly, he must resign. Thus, the primary responsibility of the Chief Minister is towards the State Legislative Assembly.

question: Who is the highest law officer in a state? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (07/08/2025) Shift 1)
options: Legal Advisor
Attorney General
Law Secretary
Advocate General
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Advocate General

Explanation:
As per Article 165 of the Indian Constitution, the highest law officer of a state is the Advocate General. They are appointed by the Governor of the state. The Advocate General advises the state government on legal matters and appears on behalf of the state in all courts within the state. They are the chief legal advisor to the state government. The position of Advocate General is analogous to the Attorney General at the central level. The Governor administers the oath of office to the Advocate General. The Advocate General can participate in any legal proceedings of the state government.

question: Under the Government of India Act, 1919, which subjects were transferred to Indian ministers?  (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (07/08/2025) Shift 2)
options: Police and Revenue
Judiciary and Foreign Affairs
Education and Health
Defence and Railways
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Education and Health

Explanation:
The Government of India Act, 1919 introduced the system of dyarchy, dividing subjects into two lists: reserved (under Governor's control) and transferred (under Indian ministers). Subjects like education, health, local self-government and agriculture were transferred, while police, revenue, judiciary and defence remained reserved. This act laid the foundation for responsible government at the provincial level, though it had many limitations.

question: Who was the first Chief Election Commissioner of India?  (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (07/08/2025) Shift 2)
options: Sukumar Sen
V Narahari Rao
HK Kripalani
MC Setalvad
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Sukumar Sen

Explanation:
The first Chief Election Commissioner of India was Sukumar Sen, who assumed office on 21 March 1950. He was responsible for conducting the first general elections in 1951-52. The Election Commission was formed under Article 324 of the Constitution. V. Narahari Rao was the first Governor of the Reserve Bank of India, while H. K. Kripalani was a prominent freedom fighter. M. C. Setalvad was the first Attorney General of India. Sukumar Sen laid the foundation of the Election Commission and ensured free and fair elections.

question: In which list of the Seventh Schedule does the Central Government have exclusive power to legislate?  (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (07/08/2025) Shift 2)
options: State List
Concurrent List
Union List
Residual List
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Union List

Explanation:
The Seventh Schedule of the Indian Constitution contains three lists: Union List, State List, and Concurrent List. The Union List includes 100 subjects (originally 97) on which only the Central Government can legislate. These subjects include defense, foreign affairs, atomic energy, railways, national highways, currency, and communication. The State List has 61 subjects for state legislatures, and the Concurrent List has 52 subjects where both central and state governments can legislate, with central law prevailing in case of conflict. The residual powers lie with Parliament but are not a separate list. Thus, the Central Government's exclusive power to legislate is over the subjects in the Union List.

☛ Total subjects in State List → 61
☛ Total subjects in Concurrent List → 52
☛ Residual powers vested with → Parliament
☛ Basis of Seventh Schedule → Federal structure

question: The National Multidimensional Poverty Index, published by NITI Aayog, measures poverty beyond income by considering multiple deprivations. Which of the following dimensions is NOT included in India's National Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI)?  (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (07/08/2025) Shift 2)
options: Education
Employment
Health
Standard of living
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Employment

Explanation:
India's National Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI) is published by NITI Aayog. It measures poverty beyond income and is based on three key dimensions: Education, Health, and Standard of Living. Each dimension includes several indicators, such as years of schooling and school attendance for education; nutrition and child mortality for health; and cooking fuel, sanitation, drinking water, electricity, housing, and assets for standard of living. Employment is not a dimension of this index. The MPI captures multidimensional aspects of poverty but does not separately include employment.

question: Which Schedule of the Constitution deals with the administration of Scheduled Areas and Tribes?  (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (07/08/2025) Shift 2)
options: Sixth Schedule
Fifth Schedule
Eleventh Schedule
Ninth Schedule
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Fifth Schedule

Explanation:
The Fifth Schedule of the Indian Constitution deals with the administration of Scheduled Areas and Scheduled Tribes. It comes under Article 244(1) and contains special provisions for the declaration, administration, and welfare of Scheduled Areas and tribes. Under this schedule, the Governor has special powers to make regulations for the peace and good governance of these areas, ensuring the protection of tribal interests. In contrast, the Sixth Schedule applies to tribal areas in northeastern states like Assam, Meghalaya, Mizoram, and Tripura. The Eleventh Schedule deals with Panchayati Raj, and the Ninth Schedule covers land reforms and other laws. Thus, the Fifth Schedule is the correct answer.

☛ The Ninth Schedule deals with what? → Land reforms and other laws

पांचवीं अनुसूची
ग्यारहवीं अनुसूची
नौवीं अनुसूची
solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है पांचवीं अनुसूची

Explanation:
भारतीय संविधान की पांचवीं अनुसूची अनुसूचित क्षेत्रों और अनुसूचित जनजातियों के प्रशासन से संबंधित है। यह अनुसूची अनुच्छेद 244(1) के अंतर्गत आती है और इसमें अनुसूचित क्षेत्रों की घोषणा, प्रशासन, और आदिवासी कल्याण के लिए विशेष प्रावधान हैं। इसके तहत राज्यपाल को अनुसूचित क्षेत्रों के प्रशासन में विशेष शक्तियां प्राप्त हैं, और वह अनुसूचित जनजातियों के हितों की रक्षा के लिए नियम बना सकते हैं। वहीं, छठी अनुसूची पूर्वोत्तर राज्यों (असम, मेघालय, मिजोरम, त्रिपुरा) के जनजातीय क्षेत्रों के प्रशासन से संबंधित है। ग्यारहवीं अनुसूची पंचायती राज से और नौवीं अनुसूची भूमि सुधार एवं अन्य कानूनों से संबंधित है। इसलिए, पांचवीं अनुसूची सही उत्तर है।

question: Which of the following is the correct descending order of ministerial ranks in the Union Council of Ministers, as per Indian practice? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (07/08/2025) Shift 3)
options: Cabinet Minister → Deputy Minister → Minister of State
Minister of State → Cabinet Minister → Deputy Minister
Deputy Minister → Minister of State → Cabinet Minister
Cabinet Minister → Minister of State → Deputy Minister
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Cabinet Minister → Minister of State → Deputy Minister

Explanation:
According to Indian practice, the descending order of ministerial ranks in the Union Council of Ministers is as follows. The highest rank is Cabinet Minister, who heads important departments and is a member of the cabinet. Next is Minister of State, who may hold independent charge or assist a Cabinet Minister. The lowest rank is Deputy Minister, who assists Ministers of State or Cabinet Ministers. This hierarchy is based on constitutional provisions and established practice under Article 75 of the Indian Constitution.

question: Which British law was a major influence on the Indian Constitution’s institutional framework? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (07/08/2025) Shift 3)
options: Government of India Act, 1935
Rowlatt Act, 1919
Indian Councils Act, 1909
Indian Independence Act, 1947
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Government of India Act, 1935

Explanation:
The institutional framework of the Indian Constitution was heavily influenced by the Government of India Act, 1935. This Act provided key provisions like a federal structure, provincial autonomy, a bicameral legislature, and an independent judiciary. The Constitution borrowed several features from this Act, such as the powers of the Governor, the Council of Ministers, the Public Service Commission, and financial relations between the centre and provinces. It served as the foundational document for India's constitutional development and was the primary source for the framers of the Constitution.

☛ Federal system model → Derived from this Act
☛ Provincial autonomy → Granted greater powers to provinces

question: To control over district courts and subordinate judiciary lies with which of the following? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (07/08/2025) Shift 3)
options: President of India
High Court
State Government
Supreme Court of India
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is High Court

Explanation:
According to Article 235 of the Indian Constitution, control over district courts and subordinate judiciary lies with the High Court. This means that matters such as appointment, promotion, transfer, and discipline of judges of subordinate courts fall under the jurisdiction of the High Court. This control is essential to maintain the independence of the judiciary. While the state government is involved in some administrative aspects, the primary authority rests with the High Court. This provision ensures that the subordinate judiciary functions effectively and impartially.

question: To pass a Constitutional Amendment Bill in the Lok Sabha, which of the following correctly states the minimum support required? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (07/08/2025) Shift 3)
options: Two-thirds majority of the total membership of the House
Simple majority of Lok Sabha members and two-thirds of Rajya Sabha members present and voting
Unanimous vote of all Members of Parliament
Majority of the total membership and two-thirds of members present and voting
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Majority of the total membership and two-thirds of members present and voting

Explanation:
As per Article 368 of the Indian Constitution, a Constitutional Amendment Bill requires the fulfillment of two conditions for passage in each House of Parliament. First, the bill must be supported by a majority of the total membership of that House. This means that more than half of the total members of the House must vote in favor of the bill. Second, the bill must be supported by a two-thirds majority of the members present and voting. This special majority ensures broad consensus for the amendment. Thus, both conditions must be satisfied simultaneously for the bill to pass. Option 1 only requires a two-thirds majority of total membership, which is incorrect. Option 2 incorrectly combines a simple majority in Lok Sabha with two-thirds in Rajya Sabha. Option 3 demands a unanimous vote, which is not constitutionally required.

☛ What type of majority is required for Constitutional Amendment? → Majority of total membership and two-thirds of members present and voting
☛ What majority is needed to pass a Money Bill? → Simple majority
☛ What is the procedure for Constitutional Amendment in Rajya Sabha? → Same dual condition as Lok Sabha
☛ Is President's prior assent required for a Constitutional Amendment Bill? → No, but President's assent is required after passage
question_hi: लोकसभा में एक संवैधानिक संशोधन विधेयक पारित करने के लिए, निम्नलिखित में से कौन सा आवश्यक न्यूनतम समर्थन को सही ढंग से बताता है? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (07/08/2025) Shift 3)
options_hi: सदन की कुल सदस्यता का दो-तिहाई बहुमत
लोकसभा सदस्यों का साधारण बहुमत और राज्यसभा के दो-तिहाई सदस्य उपस्थित और मतदान
संसद के सभी सदस्यों का सर्वसम्मत मत
कुल सदस्यता का बहुमत और उपस्थित और मतदान करने वाले सदस्यों का दो-तिहाई बहुमत
solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है कुल सदस्यता का बहुमत और उपस्थित और मतदान करने वाले सदस्यों का दो-तिहाई बहुमत

Explanation:
भारतीय संविधान के अनुच्छेद 368 के अनुसार, किसी संवैधानिक संशोधन विधेयक को पारित करने के लिए दो शर्तें पूरी होनी चाहिए। पहली शर्त यह है कि विधेयक को प्रत्येक सदन की कुल सदस्यता के बहुमत द्वारा समर्थित होना चाहिए। इसका अर्थ है कि विधेयक के पक्ष में सदन के कुल सदस्यों में से आधे से अधिक का मत होना आवश्यक है। दूसरी शर्त यह है कि विधेयक को उपस्थित और मतदान करने वाले सदस्यों के दो-तिहाई बहुमत द्वारा भी समर्थित होना चाहिए। यह विशेष बहुमत सुनिश्चित करता है कि संशोधन को व्यापक समर्थन प्राप्त हो। इस प्रकार, एक संवैधानिक संशोधन विधेयक के पारित होने के लिए दोनों शर्तों का एक साथ पूरा होना आवश्यक है। अन्य विकल्पों में से विकल्प 1 में केवल कुल सदस्यता का दो-तिहाई बहुमत मांगा गया है, जो गलत है। विकल्प 2 में दोनों सदनों के अलग-अलग बहुमत का मिश्रण है, जो सही नहीं है। विकल्प 3 सर्वसम्मति मांगता है, जो संवैधानिक रूप से आवश्यक नहीं है।

question: Which of the following was the first state to be formed on linguistic basis after severe agitation and the death of a protester?  (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (07/08/2025) Shift 3)
options: Telangana
Kerala
Andhra Pradesh
Tamil Nadu
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Andhra Pradesh

Explanation:
Andhra Pradesh was the first state to be formed on a linguistic basis. The creation of Andhra State in 1953, carved out of the Madras State, followed the death of Potti Sriramulu on 15 December 1952 after a 58-day hunger strike demanding a separate state for Telugu-speaking people. His death sparked widespread protests, forcing the Indian government to announce the formation of a linguistic state. This event set a precedent for the reorganization of states along linguistic lines, culminating in the States Reorganisation Act of 1956, which redefined state boundaries. Andhra Pradesh thus became the first state created primarily due to linguistic agitation.

question: Under the Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987, Lok Adalats have no jurisdiction to settle which of the following cases? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (08/08/2025) Shift 1)
options: Civil disputes pending in court
Divorce and non-compoundable criminal cases
Motor accident claims
Compoundable criminal offences
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Divorce and non-compoundable criminal cases

Explanation:
Under the Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987, Lok Adalats have jurisdiction only over cases that are compoundable or can be resolved through mutual settlement. Non-compoundable criminal offenses (e.g., murder, robbery) and divorce proceedings, which involve personal law and may not always be resolved by compromise, are excluded from their purview. Lok Adalats can handle civil disputes pending in court, motor accident claims, and compoundable criminal offenses (e.g., minor assault). Therefore, divorce and non-compoundable crimes are not within the jurisdiction of Lok Adalats.

☛ Appeal against Lok Adalat decision → No appeal lies against any Lok Adalat decision.

question: Which of the following Acts marked the beginning of British parliamentary control over the East India Company? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (08/08/2025) Shift 1)

question: Which of the following Directive Principles of State Policy is provided under Article 43A of the Indian Constitution? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (08/08/2025) Shift 1)
options: Right to education
Promotion of international peace
Living wage for workers
Participation of workers in industrial management
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Participation of workers in industrial management

Explanation:
Article 43A of the Indian Constitution directs the State to take steps to secure the participation of workers in the management of industries by suitable legislation or other means. It is one of the Directive Principles of State Policy included in Part IV of the Constitution. This article was added by the 42nd Amendment (1976). Its objective is to promote industrial democracy by involving workers in decision-making processes. Right to education is covered under Article 21A, promotion of international peace under Article 51, and living wage for workers under Article 43.

question: Article 19 of the Indian Constitution guarantees six freedoms. Which of the following is NOT one of them? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (08/08/2025) Shift 1)
options: Freedom to form associations or unions
Freedom from arrest
Freedom of speech and expression
Freedom to move freely throughout the territory of India
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Freedom from arrest

Explanation:
Article 19 provides six freedoms: (1) speech and expression, (2) peaceful assembly without arms, (3) forming associations/unions, (4) moving freely throughout India, (5) residing anywhere, (6) practicing any profession or occupation. 'Freedom from arrest' is covered under Article 22, not Article 19. It is part of the right to personal liberty under Articles 21 and 22. The six freedoms under Article 19 can be reasonably restricted in the interest of sovereignty, security, public order, decency, etc.

question: Which Article provides for the formation of Ward Committees in Municipal areas? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (08/08/2025) Shift 1)
options: Article 243R
Article 243Z
Article 243T
Article 243S
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Article 243S

Explanation:
Article 243S of the Indian Constitution provides for the formation of Ward Committees in Municipal areas. This article was added by the 74th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992, which deals with municipalities. According to this provision, Ward Committees are mandatory in municipal areas with a population of 3 lakh or more. A Ward Committee may consist of one or more wards, as determined by the state legislature. This committee ensures public participation in municipal functioning and helps address local issues. The municipal provisions are covered under Part IXA of the Constitution, spanning Articles 243P to 243ZG.

question: Which Act created the post of the Governor-General of Bengal? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (08/08/2025) Shift 2)
options: Regulating Act, 1773
Pitt’s India Act, 1784
Government of India Act, 1858
Charter Act, 1813
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Regulating Act, 1773

Explanation:
The Regulating Act of 1773 was the first law passed by the British Parliament to regulate the affairs of the East India Company in India. This act created the post of Governor-General of Bengal and appointed Warren Hastings as the first Governor-General. It unified the administration of Bengal, Bihar, and Odisha. It also established a Supreme Court and provided the Governor-General with a four-member Executive Council. The act was a major step towards centralized control of British territories in India.

question: Which of the following Parliamentary Committees of India is considered a ‘Financial Committee’?  (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (08/08/2025) Shift 2)
options: Committee on Welfare of SCs and STs

Committee on Privileges
Estimates Committee
solution:

Explanation:
The Indian Parliament has three Financial Committees: Estimates Committee, Public Accounts Committee, and Committee on Public Undertakings. The Estimates Committee was established in 1950 and consists of 30 members, all from Lok Sabha. Its main function is to examine government budget estimates and suggest efficiencies. Among the other options, the Committee on Welfare of SCs and STs, Committee on Petitions, and Committee on Privileges are not financial committees.

नागरिकता (संशोधन) अधिनियम, 2019 के अनुसार, पाकिस्तान, अफगानिस्तान और बांग्लादेश से धार्मिक उत्पीड़न के कारण भारत आने वाले हिंदू, सिख, बौद्ध, जैन, पारसी और ईसाई समुदायों के लिए नागरिकता प्राप्त करने की अवधि 11 वर्ष से घटाकर 6 वर्ष कर दी गई है। इस अधिनियम में केवल इन तीन देशों के छह धार्मिक समुदायों को शामिल किया गया है। नेपाल, श्रीलंका, इजराइल आदि देशों के लिए यह प्रावधान लागू नहीं है। इसलिए पाकिस्तान से सिख समुदाय 6 वर्ष के निवास के बाद नागरिकता के लिए आवेदन कर सकता है।

question: Under which of the following conditions is a Tribal Advisory Council (TAC) established in a State? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (08/08/2025) Shift 2)
options: When the tribal population exceeds 10%
When the tribal population exceeds 50%
If the State has any forest area
If there is at least one Scheduled Tribe
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is If there is at least one Scheduled Tribe.

Explanation:
A Tribal Advisory Council (TAC) is established in a state when there is at least one Scheduled Tribe residing in that state. This provision is given in the Fifth Schedule under Article 244(1) of the Indian Constitution. The TAC is constituted by the Governor and consists of 20 members, out of which three-fourths are representatives of the Scheduled Tribes. Its main objective is to advise the Governor on the administration and welfare of tribal areas.

question: Under Article 239 of the Constitution, a Union Territory is administered by: (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (08/08/2025) Shift 3)
options: the Governor of an adjacent State
the Prime Minister of India
the Parliament of India
the President of India
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is the President of India

Explanation:
Under Article 239, every Union Territory is administered by the President of India. The President exercises these powers through an Administrator or Lieutenant Governor appointed by him. This provision reflects the special status of Union Territories, where the Parliament can directly legislate. However, some Union Territories like Delhi and Puducherry have partial statehood with elected legislatures and councils of ministers. The President's role under Article 239 ensures central government control over these territories.

☛ Who makes laws for Union Territories? → Parliament
question_hi: संविधान के अनुच्छेद 239 के तहत, एक केंद्र शासित प्रदेश किसके द्वारा प्रशासित होता है: (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (08/08/2025) Shift 3)

भारत के राष्ट्रपति
solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है भारत के राष्ट्रपति

Explanation:
अनुच्छेद 239 के अनुसार, प्रत्येक केंद्र शासित प्रदेश का प्रशासन राष्ट्रपति द्वारा किया जाता है। राष्ट्रपति अपनी शक्तियों का प्रयोग प्रशासक या उपराज्यपाल के माध्यम से करता है, जिसे वह नियुक्त करता है। यह प्रावधान केंद्र शासित प्रदेशों की विशेष स्थिति को दर्शाता है, जहां संसद सीधे कानून बना सकती है। हालांकि, दिल्ली और पुदुचेरी जैसे कुछ केंद्र शासित प्रदेशों को आंशिक राज्य का दर्जा प्राप्त है, जहां निर्वाचित विधानसभा और मंत्रिपरिषद होती है। अनुच्छेद 239 के तहत राष्ट्रपति की भूमिका केंद्र सरकार के नियंत्रण को सुनिश्चित करती है।
